sentences.zh: 太宗因修禮官奏事之次，言及喪服，太宗曰：「又舅之與姨，親疏相似，而服紀有殊，理未為得。宜集學者詳議。餘有親重而服輕者，亦附奏聞。」於是侍中魏徵、禮部侍郎令狐德棻等奏議曰：臣聞禮所以決嫌疑，定猶豫，別同異，明是非者也。非從天降，非從地出，人情而已矣。夫親族有九，服術有六，隨恩以薄厚，稱情以立文。然舅之與姨，雖為同氣，論情度義，先後實殊。何則？舅為母之本族，姨乃外戚他族，求之母族，姨不在焉，考之經典，舅誠為重。故周王念齊，每稱舅甥之國；秦伯懷晉，實切《渭陽》之詩。在舅服止一時，為姨居喪五月，循名喪實，逐末棄本。蓋古人之情，或有未達，所宜損益，實在茲乎！《記》曰：「兄弟之子，猶子也。蓋引而進之也；嫂叔之不服，蓋推而遠之也。」禮：繼父同居，則為之期；未嘗同居，則不為服。從母之夫，舅之妻，二夫人相為服。或曰，同爨緦。然則繼父之徒，並非骨肉，服重由乎同爨，恩輕在乎異居。故知制服雖繫於名；亦緣恩之厚薄者也。或有長年之嫂，遇孩童之叔，劬勞鞠養，情若新生，分飢共寒，契闊偕老。譬同居之繼父，方他人之同爨，情義之深淺，寧可同日而言哉！在其生也，愛之同於骨肉；及其死也，則曰推而遠之。求之本原，深所未諭。若推而遠之為是，則不可生而共居；生而共居之為是，則不可死同行路。重其生而輕其死，厚其始而薄其終，稱情立文，其義安在？且事嫂見稱，載籍非一。鄭仲虞則恩禮甚篤，顏弘都則竭誠致感，馬援則見之必冠，孔伋則哭之為位。此並躬踐教義，仁深孝友，察其所尚之旨，豈非先覺者歟？但於其時，上無哲王，禮非下之所議，遂使深情郁乎千載，至理藏於萬古，其來久矣，豈不惜哉！今屬欽明在辰，聖人有作，五禮詳洽，一物無遺。猶且永念慎終，凝神遐想。以為尊卑之敘，雖煥乎大備；喪紀之制，或情理未周。爰命秩宗，更詳考正。臣等奏遵明旨，觸類旁求，採摭群經，討論傳記。或引兼名實，無文之禮咸秩，惇睦之情畢舉，變薄俗於既往，垂篤義於將來，信六籍所不能談，超百王而獨得者也。諸儒所守，互有異同，詳求厥中，申明聖旨。謹按曾祖父母舊服齊衰三月，請加為齊衰五月。嫡子婦舊服大功，請加為期。眾子婦小功，今請與兄弟子婦同為大功九月。嫂叔舊無服，今請服小功五月報。其弟妻及夫兄，亦小功五月。舅服緦麻，請與從母同服小功。

translations.literal: While Taizong was hearing the ritual-revision officers report on business, the subject reached mourning dress. Taizong said: "Also, maternal uncles and maternal aunts are similar in closeness, yet the mourning regulations differ for them; in principle this does not seem right. Scholars should be assembled to deliberate on it in detail. Other cases where kinship is heavy but mourning is light should also be appended and reported." Thereupon Palace Attendant Wei Zheng, Vice Minister of Rites Linghu Defen, and others memorialized in deliberation: Your servants have heard that ritual is what resolves doubts and suspicions, settles hesitations, distinguishes sameness and difference, and clarifies right and wrong. It does not descend from Heaven or emerge from earth; it is simply human feeling. Kin have nine degrees and mourning techniques have six, thinning or thickening according to affection and establishing the text according to feeling. Yet although maternal uncle and maternal aunt are of the same breath, when feeling is discussed and obligation measured, the former and latter are truly different. Why? The maternal uncle belongs to the mother's root clan, while the maternal aunt is an external relative of another clan. Seeking within the mother's clan, the maternal aunt is not there; examining the classics, the maternal uncle is truly weighty. Therefore when the Zhou king remembered Qi, he always called it the state of uncle and nephew; when the Earl of Qin cherished Jin, it was truly close to the poem Weiyang. For a maternal uncle, mourning stops at one season; for a maternal aunt, one mourns five months. This follows the name and loses the substance, pursuing the branch and abandoning the root. The feeling of the ancients perhaps had something not yet fully reached, and what should be reduced or increased truly lies here. The Record says: "The sons of brothers are like sons; this draws them in and advances them. That elder-brother's wife and younger-brother-in-law do not mourn each other pushes them away." In ritual, for a stepfather who has lived with one, one wears one-year mourning; if he has never lived with one, one wears no mourning. A mother's sister's husband and a maternal uncle's wife, these two spouses mourn one another. Some say that those who share the cooking hearth wear fine hemp. Thus stepfathers and such are not flesh and blood, yet mourning is heavy because of sharing the hearth, and affection is light because of living apart. Therefore we know that although mourning dress depends on names, it also follows the thickness or thinness of affection. Sometimes there is an elder sister-in-law of advanced years with a younger brother-in-law who was a child; she toiled to raise him, with feeling as if newly giving birth, sharing hunger and cold, and staying with him through hardship into old age. Compared with a stepfather who shared the household or with another person sharing the cooking hearth, how could the depth or shallowness of feeling and obligation be discussed on the same day? While she lives, he loves her as flesh and blood; when she dies, one says she is pushed away. Seeking the root of this, we deeply fail to understand it. If pushing away is right, then they should not live together while alive. If living together while alive is right, then they cannot be treated as people on the road when dead. To value the living and slight the dead, to thicken the beginning and thin the end: where is the meaning of matching feeling and establishing text? Moreover, serving a sister-in-law is praised in more than one written record. Zheng Zhongyu's grace and ritual were very deep; Yan Hongdu exhausted sincerity and produced a response; Ma Yuan always put on his cap when seeing his sister-in-law; Kong Ji cried for his sister-in-law with a set position. These all personally practiced teaching and obligation, with benevolence deep in filial and fraternal feeling. Examining the purpose of what they honored, were they not those who awakened first? Only in their time there was no wise king above, and ritual was not for those below to debate; thus deep feeling was suppressed for a thousand years, and perfect principle was hidden for ten thousand ages. This has been so for a long time; is it not regrettable? Now we meet a time when reverent brightness is present and a sage has arisen. The five rites are detailed and complete, with not one thing omitted. Still Your Majesty forever thinks on careful endings and concentrates spirit in distant reflection, considering that although the sequence of honored and lowly is bright and fully prepared, the regulations of mourning may not yet be complete in feeling and principle. Therefore you ordered the Minister of Rites to examine and correct them in more detail. Your servants, in memorializing, follow the bright command, seek sideways by analogy, gather from the many classics, and discuss commentaries and records. Some cases draw on both name and substance; rites without written text are all ordered, and the feeling of generous harmony is fully raised, changing thin customs from the past and transmitting deep obligation to the future. This is truly what the six classics could not discuss and what surpasses the hundred kings as Your Majesty's sole attainment. The various scholars hold to different views. We have sought the center in detail and extend and clarify the sage command. Respectfully, the old mourning for great-grandparents was three months of trimmed mourning; we request increasing it to five months of trimmed mourning. The old mourning for the principal son's wife was great-work mourning; we request increasing it to one year. The mourning for wives of other sons was small-work mourning; we now request making it the same as for brothers' sons' wives, great-work mourning for nine months. Elder-brother's wife and younger-brother-in-law formerly had no mourning; we now request reciprocal small-work mourning for five months. The younger brother's wife and her husband's elder brother should also have small-work mourning for five months. Mourning for a maternal uncle was fine hemp; we request making it the same as for a mother's sister, small-work mourning.

sentences.zh: 制可之。

translations.literal: The ordinance approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 顯慶二年九月，修禮官長孫無忌等又奏曰：「依古喪服，甥為舅緦麻，舅報甥亦同此制。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianqing, in the ninth month, rites-revising officials Zhangsun Wuji and others again memorialized, saying: "According to ancient mourning dress, a nephew for his mother's brother wears three months' finest hemp; the mother's brother's return mourning for the nephew follows the same rule.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianqing, in the ninth month, rites-revising officials Zhangsun Wuji and others again memorialized, saying: "According to ancient mourning dress, a nephew for his mother's brother wears three months' finest hemp; the mother's brother's return mourning for the nephew follows the same rule.

sentences.zh: 貞觀年中，八座議奏：『舅服同姨，小功五月。』

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era the Eight Seats deliberated and memorialized: 'For the mother's brother, mourning is the same as for the mother's sister—five months' lesser accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan the Eight Seats had ruled that mourning for a mother's brother matched that for a mother's sister: five months' lesser accomplishment.

sentences.zh: 而今律疏，舅報於甥，服猶三月。

translations.literal: Yet in the present Code and Commentaries, the mother's brother's return mourning toward the nephew is still three months.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the current Code and Commentaries still fixed the uncle's return mourning for a nephew at three months.

sentences.zh: 謹按旁尊之服，禮無不報，已非正尊，不敢降也。

translations.literal: We respectfully note that for mourning toward collateral elders, ritual never lacks return mourning; though they are not primary elders, one dare not reduce it.
translations.idiomatic: Collateral elders always received return mourning in ritual; though not primary kin, the grade must not be cut.

sentences.zh: 故甥為從母五月，從母報甥小功，甥為舅緦麻，舅亦報甥三月，是其義矣。

translations.literal: Thus a nephew for the mother's sister wears five months; the mother's sister's return for the nephew is lesser accomplishment; a nephew for the mother's brother wears finest hemp; the mother's brother also returns finest hemp for the nephew three months—that is the principle.
translations.idiomatic: So a nephew wore five months for a mother's sister, and she returned lesser accomplishment; for a mother's brother he wore finest hemp, and the uncle returned three months' finest hemp—that was the pattern.

sentences.zh: 今甥為舅使同從母之喪，則舅宜進甥以同從母之報。

translations.literal: Now if a nephew for his mother's brother is made the same as mourning for the mother's sister, then the mother's brother ought to advance his return for the nephew to match the mother's sister's return.
translations.idiomatic: If a nephew's mourning for his mother's brother was raised to match a mother's sister, the uncle's return mourning for the nephew should rise to match her return as well.

sentences.zh: 修律疏人不知禮意，舅報甥服，尚止緦麻，於例不通，禮須改正。

translations.literal: Those who revised the Code and Commentaries did not know ritual intent; the mother's brother's return mourning for the nephew still stopping at finest hemp is inconsistent with precedent and ritual must be corrected.
translations.idiomatic: The Code revisers had missed the point: leaving the uncle's return at finest hemp broke precedent and had to be fixed.

sentences.zh: 今請修改律疏，舅報甥亦功。」

translations.literal: We now request revision of the Code and Commentaries so that the mother's brother's return mourning for the nephew is also lesser accomplishment."
translations.idiomatic: We now request revision of the Code and Commentaries so that the mother's brother's return mourning for the nephew is also lesser accomplishment."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「庶母古禮緦麻，新禮無服。

translations.literal: They also said: "In ancient ritual a secondary mother was finest hemp; in the new ritual there is no mourning.
translations.idiomatic: They also said: "In ancient ritual a secondary mother was finest hemp; in the new ritual there is no mourning.

sentences.zh: 謹按庶母之子，即是己昆季，為之杖期，而己與之無服。

translations.literal: We respectfully note that sons of a secondary mother are one's own brothers and sisters; for them one wears staff for one year, yet for the secondary mother oneself wears none.
translations.idiomatic: Sons of a secondary mother were full siblings: one wore staff for a year for them, yet wore nothing for the secondary mother herself.

sentences.zh: 同氣之內，吉凶頓殊，求之禮情，深非至理。

translations.literal: Within the same breath, fortune and misfortune suddenly differ—sought in ritual feeling, this is deeply not ultimate reason.
translations.idiomatic: Within one flesh, joy and grief were graded worlds apart—a poor fit to ritual feeling.

sentences.zh: 請依典故，為服緦麻。」

translations.literal: We request that according to ancient precedent mourning of finest hemp be worn."
translations.idiomatic: We request that according to ancient precedent mourning of finest hemp be worn."

sentences.zh: 制又從之。

translations.literal: The ordinance again approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved again.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年八月，所司奏：「司文正卿蕭嗣業，嫡繼母改嫁身亡，請申心制。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo, in the eighth month the relevant office memorialized: "Director of Literary Affairs Xiao Siye's legitimate stepmother remarried and died; he requests to declare heart mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Longshuo, in the eighth month the relevant office memorialized: "Director of Literary Affairs Xiao Siye's legitimate stepmother remarried and died; he requests to declare heart mourning.

sentences.zh: 據令，繼母改嫁及為長子，並不解官。」

translations.literal: According to the ordinance, a stepmother's remarriage and being the eldest son both do not require leaving office."
translations.idiomatic: According to the ordinance, a stepmother's remarriage and being the eldest son both do not require leaving office."

sentences.zh: 既而有敕：「雖云嫡母，終是繼母，據禮緣情，須有定制。付所司議定奏聞。」司禮太常伯隴西郡王博乂等奏稱：緬尋《喪服》，母名斯定，嫡、繼、慈、養，皆在其中。惟出母制，特言出妻之子，明非生己，則皆無服。是以令云母嫁，又云出妻之子。出言其子，以著所生，嫁即言母，通包養、嫡，俱當解任，併合心喪。其不解者，惟有繼母之嫁。繼母為名，正據前妻之子；嫡於諸孽，禮無繼母之文。甲令今既見行，嗣業理申心制。然奉敕議定，方垂永則，令有不安，亦須釐正。竊以嫡、繼、慈、養，皆非所生，並同行路。嫁雖比出稍輕，於父終為義絕。繼母之嫁，既殊親母，慈、嫡義絕，豈合心喪？望請凡非所生，父卒而嫁，為父後者無服，非承重者杖期，並不心喪，一同繼母。有符情禮，無玷舊章。又心喪之制，惟施服屈，杖期之服，不應解官。而令文三年齊斬，亦入心喪之例；杖期解官，又有妻喪之舛。又依禮，庶子為其母緦麻三月。既是所生母服，准例亦合解官。令文漏而不言，於事終須修附。既與嫡母等嫁同一令條，總議請改，理為允愜者。依集文武官九品已上議。得司衛正卿房仁裕等七百三十六人議，請一依司禮狀，嗣業不解官。得右金吾衛將軍薛孤吳仁等二十六人議，請解嗣業官，不同司禮狀者。母非所生，出嫁義絕，仍令解職，有紊緣情。杖期解官，不甄妻服，三年齊斬，謬曰心喪。庶子為母緦麻，漏其中制。此並令文疏舛，理難因襲。依房仁裕等議，總加修附，垂之不朽。其禮及律疏有相關涉者，亦請准此改正。嗣業既非嫡母改醮，不合解官。

translations.literal: An edict followed: "Although she is called a legitimate mother, in the end she is a stepmother. According to ritual and following feeling, there must be a fixed rule. Send this to the responsible office to deliberate and determine, then memorialize." Bo Yi, Director of Ceremonies and Chamberlain for Ceremonials, Prince of Longxi Commandery, and others memorialized: Searching deeply in the Mourning Dress, the name mother is fixed, and legitimate, step-, compassionate, and adoptive mothers are all included within it. Only in the rule for a divorced mother does it specifically say "the son of a divorced wife," making clear that if she did not give birth to him, there is no mourning for all such cases. Therefore the code says "when a mother remarries," and also says "the son of a divorced wife." When it says "divorced," it mentions her son to show the one she bore; when it says "remarries," it says mother and broadly includes adoptive and legitimate mothers. All should leave office and observe inner mourning. The only one who does not leave office is a stepmother who remarries. The name stepmother properly refers to the son of a former wife; for the legitimate wife in relation to concubine-born sons, ritual has no text calling her stepmother. Since the statute is now in force, Siye may in principle extend inner mourning. Yet since an edict orders determination so that it may become a permanent rule, if the statute has something unsettled, it must also be corrected. Privately we think that legitimate, step-, compassionate, and adoptive mothers are all not the birth mother and are all the same as people on the road. Though remarriage is slightly lighter than divorce, in relation to the father it is still a severing of obligation. Since remarriage of a stepmother differs from the birth mother, and the obligation to a compassionate or legitimate mother is severed, how should inner mourning apply? We request that whenever the woman is not the birth mother and, after the father dies, she remarries, the one who succeeds as heir to the father should have no mourning for her, while one who does not bear the main succession should observe staff-year mourning, and none should observe inner mourning, all being the same as with a stepmother. This accords with feeling and ritual and does not blemish the old statutes. Also, the rule of inner mourning applies only when mourning dress is reduced; staff-year mourning should not require leaving office. Yet the code text puts three-year mourning with trimmed and unhemmed garments also under inner mourning; staff-year mourning requiring leaving office also has the error of a wife's mourning. Again according to ritual, a concubine-born son mourns his mother with fine hemp for three months. Since this is mourning for the birth mother, by precedent he should also leave office. The code omits this and does not say it, but in practice it must ultimately be amended. Since it is in the same statute as remarriage of a legitimate mother, we request that all these points be revised together, which in principle is fitting. The matter was referred to assembled civil and military officials of the ninth rank and above for deliberation. The opinion of Fang Renyu, Chief Minister of the Guard, and 736 others was obtained, requesting full adherence to the Director of Ceremonies' statement and that Siye not leave office. The opinion of Xuegu Wuren, General of the Right Gold Bird Guard, and twenty-six others was obtained, requesting that Siye leave office, differing from the Director of Ceremonies' statement. Since a mother who is not the birth mother severs obligation by remarrying, still ordering departure from office disrupts following feeling. Requiring departure from office for staff-year mourning, without distinguishing mourning for a wife; falsely calling three-year trimmed and unhemmed mourning inner mourning; omitting the middle rule for a concubine-born son mourning his mother in fine hemp: these are all omissions and errors in the code text and are hard in principle to carry forward. Follow the deliberation of Fang Renyu and the others, revise and add all of them, and transmit this imperishably. Where the ritual and legal commentary are related to these matters, we also request that they be corrected according to this. Since Siye's case is not remarriage of a legitimate mother, he should not leave office.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed: "Although she is called a legitimate mother, in the end she is a stepmother. According to ritual and following feeling, there must be a fixed rule. Send this to the responsible office to deliberate and determine, then memorialize." Bo Yi, Director of Ceremonies and Chamberlain for Ceremonials, Prince of Longxi Commandery, and others memorialized: Searching deeply in the Mourning Dress, the name mother is fixed, and legitimate, step-, compassionate, and adoptive mothers are all included within it. Only in the rule for a divorced mother does it specifically say "the son of a divorced wife," making clear that if she did not give birth to him, there is no mourning for all such cases. Therefore the code says "when a mother remarries," and also says "the son of a divorced wife." When it says "divorced," it mentions her son to show the one she bore; when it says "remarries," it says mother and broadly includes adoptive and legitimate mothers. All should leave office and observe inner mourning. The only one who does not leave office is a stepmother who remarries. The name stepmother properly refers to the son of a former wife; for the legitimate wife in relation to concubine-born sons, ritual has no text calling her stepmother. Since the statute is now in force, Siye may in principle extend inner mourning. Yet since an edict orders determination so that it may become a permanent rule, if the statute has something unsettled, it must also be corrected. Privately we think that legitimate, step-, compassionate, and adoptive mothers are all not the birth mother and are all the same as people on the road. Though remarriage is slightly lighter than divorce, in relation to the father it is still a severing of obligation. Since remarriage of a stepmother differs from the birth mother, and the obligation to a compassionate or legitimate mother is severed, how should inner mourning apply? We request that whenever the woman is not the birth mother and, after the father dies, she remarries, the one who succeeds as heir to the father should have no mourning for her, while one who does not bear the main succession should observe staff-year mourning, and none should observe inner mourning, all being the same as with a stepmother. This accords with feeling and ritual and does not blemish the old statutes. Also, the rule of inner mourning applies only when mourning dress is reduced; staff-year mourning should not require leaving office. Yet the code text puts three-year mourning with trimmed and unhemmed garments also under inner mourning; staff-year mourning requiring leaving office also has the error of a wife's mourning. Again according to ritual, a concubine-born son mourns his mother with fine hemp for three months. Since this is mourning for the birth mother, by precedent he should also leave office. The code omits this and does not say it, but in practice it must ultimately be amended. Since it is in the same statute as remarriage of a legitimate mother, we request that all these points be revised together, which in principle is fitting. The matter was referred to assembled civil and military officials of the ninth rank and above for deliberation. The opinion of Fang Renyu, Chief Minister of the Guard, and 736 others was obtained, requesting full adherence to the Director of Ceremonies' statement and that Siye not leave office. The opinion of Xuegu Wuren, General of the Right Gold Bird Guard, and twenty-six others was obtained, requesting that Siye leave office, differing from the Director of Ceremonies' statement. Since a mother who is not the birth mother severs obligation by remarrying, still ordering departure from office disrupts following feeling. Requiring departure from office for staff-year mourning, without distinguishing mourning for a wife; falsely calling three-year trimmed and unhemmed mourning inner mourning; omitting the middle rule for a concubine-born son mourning his mother in fine hemp: these are all omissions and errors in the code text and are hard in principle to carry forward. Follow the deliberation of Fang Renyu and the others, revise and add all of them, and transmit this imperishably. Where the ritual and legal commentary are related to these matters, we also request that they be corrected according to this. Since Siye's case is not remarriage of a legitimate mother, he should not leave office.

sentences.zh: 詔從之，

translations.literal: The decree approved,
translations.idiomatic: The court assented.

sentences.zh: 上元元年，天后上表曰：「至如父在為母服止一期，雖心喪三年，服由尊降。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shangyuan, Empress Wu submitted a memorial, saying: "As for when the father is alive, mourning for the mother stops at one cycle—though heart mourning is three years, the garment is reduced by reverence for the father.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shangyuan, Empress Wu submitted a memorial, saying: "As for when the father is alive, mourning for the mother stops at one cycle—though heart mourning is three years, the garment is reduced by reverence for the father.

sentences.zh: 竊謂子之於母，慈愛特深，非母不生，非母不育。

translations.literal: I venture to say that in a child's relation to the mother, affection is especially deep—without the mother one is not born, without the mother one is not reared.
translations.idiomatic: A child owes the mother a singular depth of love: without her there is no birth, without her no rearing.

sentences.zh: 推燥居濕，咽苦吐甘，生養勞瘁，恩斯極矣！

translations.literal: Tending dryness and wetness, swallowing bitterness and spitting sweetness—the toil of bearing and rearing, kindness reaches its utmost!
translations.idiomatic: She tended his dryness and wetness, swallowed bitterness and gave sweetness—the labor of nurture exhausts what kindness can mean.

sentences.zh: 所以禽獸之情，猶知其母，三年在懷，理宜崇報。

translations.literal: Therefore even beasts in feeling know their mother; three years in the womb—by principle one ought to honor her in return.
translations.idiomatic: Even beasts know their dam; three years in the womb demand a commensurate return.

sentences.zh: 若父在為母服止一期，尊父之敬雖周，報母之慈有闕。

translations.literal: If when the father is alive mourning for the mother stops at one cycle, reverence for the father is complete yet requital of the mother's kindness is lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Stopping at one cycle while the father lived honored him fully but left the mother's kindness short.

sentences.zh: 且齊斬之制，足為差減，更令周以一期，恐傷人子之志。

translations.literal: Moreover the hemmed-and-cut garment system is sufficient for graduated reduction; to make one cycle suffice where three years should apply would wound the son's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Hemmed sackcloth already graded the mourning; shrinking three years to one cycle would wound a son's intent.

sentences.zh: 今請父在為母終三年之服。」

translations.literal: We now request that when the father is alive mourning for the mother run the full three years."
translations.idiomatic: We now request that when the father is alive mourning for the mother run the full three years."

sentences.zh: 高宗下詔，依議行焉，

translations.literal: Gaozong issued a decree and followed the proposal in practice,
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong decreed and put her proposal into practice.

sentences.zh: 開元五年，右補闕盧履冰上言：「准禮，父在為母一週除靈，三年心喪。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaiyuan, Right Remonstrator Lu Lübing submitted a memorial: "According to ritual, when the father is alive, for the mother one cycle until removal of the spirit tablet, three years' heart mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Kaiyuan, Right Remonstrator Lu Lübing submitted a memorial: "According to ritual, when the father is alive, for the mother one cycle until removal of the spirit tablet, three years' heart mourning.

sentences.zh: 則天皇后請同父沒之服，三年然始除靈。

translations.literal: Empress Wu Zetian requested mourning the same as when the father is dead—three years before removal of the spirit tablet.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu had asked for the same garment as when the father was dead—three years before tablet removal.

sentences.zh: 雖則權行，有紊彝典。

translations.literal: Though it was provisionally carried out, it disorderly violated the constant canon.
translations.idiomatic: That expedient had been carried out, but it tangled the standing canon.

sentences.zh: 今陛下孝理天下，動合禮經，請仍舊章，庶葉通典。」

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty filially governs the realm and moves in accord with ritual classics; we request return to the old articles, that it may accord with the comprehensive canon."
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty filially governs the realm and moves in accord with ritual classics; we request return to the old articles, that it may accord with the comprehensive canon."

sentences.zh: 於是下制令百官詳議；

translations.literal: Thereupon a decree was issued ordering the hundred officials to deliberate in detail;
translations.idiomatic: A decree ordered the bureaucracy to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 並舅及嫂叔服不依舊禮，亦合議定。

translations.literal: mourning for mother's brothers and sisters-in-law and younger uncles not following the old ritual should also be settled by deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning for uncles, aunts, sisters-in-law, and younger uncles that no longer matched the old ritual was to be settled in the same review.

sentences.zh: 刑部郎中田再思建議曰：干尊坤卑，天一地二，陰陽之位分矣，夫婦之道配焉。至若死喪之威，隆殺之等，禮經五服之制，齊斬有殊，考妣三年之喪，貴賤無隔，以報免懷之慈，以酬罔極之恩者也。稽之上古，喪期無數，暨乎中葉，方有歲年。《禮》云：「五帝殊時，不相沿樂；三王異代，不相襲禮。」《白虎通》云：「質文再變，正朔三而復。」自周公制禮之後，孔父刊經已來，爰殊厭降之儀，以標服紀之節。重輕從俗，斟酌隨時。故知禮不從天而降，不由地而出也，在人消息，為適時之中耳。春秋諸國，魯最知禮，以周公之後，孔子之邦也。晉韓起來聘，言「周禮盡在魯矣。」齊仲孫來盟，言「魯猶秉周禮。」尚有子張問高宗諒陰三年，子思不聽其子服出母，子游謂同母異父昆弟之服大功，子夏謂合從齊衰之制。此等並四科之數，十哲之人，高步孔門，親承聖訓，及遇喪事，猶此致疑，即明自古已來，升降不一者也。三年之制，說者紛然。鄭玄以為二十七月，王肅以為二十五月。又改葬之服，鄭云服緦三月，王云訖葬而除。又繼母出嫁，鄭云皆服，王云從於繼育，乃為之服。又無服之殤，鄭云子生一月，哭之一日；王云以哭之一日易服之月。鄭、王祖經宗傳，各有異同；荀摯采古求遺，互為損益。方知去聖漸遠，殘缺彌多。故曰會禮之家，名為聚訟，寧有定哉！而父在為母三年，行之已逾四紀，出自高宗大帝之代，不從則天皇后之朝。大帝御極之辰，中宮獻書之日，往時參議，將可施行，編之於格，服之已久。前王所是，疏而為律；後王所是，著而為令。何必乖先帝之旨，阻人子之情，虧純孝之心，背德義之本？有何妨於聖化，有何紊於彝倫，而欲服之週年，與伯叔母齊焉，與姑姊妹同焉？夫三年之喪，如白駒之過隙，君子喪親，有終身之憂，何況再周乎！夫禮者，體也，履也，示之以跡。孝者，畜也，養也，因之以心。小人不恥不仁，不畏不義。服之有制，使愚人企及；衣之以衰，使見之摧痛。以此防人，人猶有朝死而夕忘者；以此制人，人猶有釋服而從吉者。方今漸歸古樸，須敦孝義，抑賢引愚，理資寧戚，食稻衣錦，所不忍聞。若以庶事朝儀，一依周禮，則古之人臣見君也，公卿大夫贄羔雁、珪璧，今何故不依乎？周之用刑也，墨、劓、宮、刖，今何故不行乎？周則侯、甸、男、衛，朝聘有數，今何故不行乎？周則不五十不仕，七十不入朝，今何故不依乎？周則井、邑、丘、甸，以立徵稅，今何故不行乎？周則三老五等，父死子及，今何故不行乎？周則冠冕衣裘，乘車而戰，今何故不行乎？周則分土五更，膠序養老，今何故不行乎？諸如此例，不可勝述。何獨孝思之事，愛一年之服於其母乎？可為痛心，可為慟哭者！《詩》云：「哀哀父母，生我劬勞。」《禮》云：「父之親子也，親賢而下無能；母之親子也，賢則親之，無能則憐之。」阮嗣宗晉代之英才，方外之高士，以為母重於父。據齊斬升數，粗細已降，何忍服之節制，減至於周？豈後代之士，盡慚於古。循古未必是，依今未必非也。又同爨服緦，禮經明義。嫂叔遠別，同諸路人。引而進之，觸類而長。猶子咸衣苴枲，季父不服緦麻，推遠之情有餘，睦親之義未足。又母之昆弟，情切渭陽，翟酺訟舅之冤，甯氏宅甥之相，我之出也，義亦殷焉。不同從母之尊，遂降小功之服，依諸古禮，有爽俗情。今貶舅而宗姨，是陋今而榮古。此並太宗之制也，行之百年矣，輒為刊復，實用有疑。

translations.literal: Tian Zaisi, Bureau Director in the Ministry of Justice, made a proposal: Qian is honored and kun is lowly; Heaven is one and earth is two. The positions of yin and yang are divided, and the way of husband and wife is paired with them. As for the awe of death and mourning and the grades of fullness and reduction, the ritual classics have the system of the five mourning grades. Trimmed and unhemmed mourning differ, but the three-year mourning for father and mother has no barrier between noble and base, because it repays the kindness of bearing and cherishing and answers boundless grace. Examining high antiquity, mourning terms had no fixed number; by middle antiquity, only then were there years and months. The Ritual says: "The Five Emperors differed in time and did not follow one another in music; the Three Kings differed in age and did not inherit one another's rites." The Baihu Tong says: "Plainness and refinement change twice, and the first month changes through three and returns." Since the Duke of Zhou made ritual and since Confucius edited the classics, there have been different rules of suppression and reduction to mark the divisions of mourning regulations. Heavy and light follow custom; deliberation and adjustment follow the time. Thus we know ritual does not descend from Heaven or come out from earth; it lies in human increase and decrease, making what fits the time and the mean. Among the states of the Spring and Autumn, Lu best knew ritual, because it was the descendants of the Duke of Zhou and the state of Confucius. When Han Qi of Jin came on a visit, he said, "The rites of Zhou are all in Lu." When Zhongsun of Qi came to make a covenant, he said, "Lu still holds the rites of Zhou." Yet Zizhang asked about Gaozong's three years of silent mourning; Zisi did not allow his son to wear mourning for his divorced mother; Ziyou said that brothers with the same mother but different fathers should wear great-work mourning; Zixia said they should follow the trimmed-mourning rule. These were all among the numbered disciples of the four categories and the ten philosophers, men of high rank in Confucius's gate who personally received the sage teaching; yet when they encountered mourning matters, they still produced doubts like this. This makes clear that since antiquity increases and reductions have not been uniform. As for the three-year system, explanations are confused. Zheng Xuan considered it twenty-seven months; Wang Su considered it twenty-five months. Again for mourning after reburial, Zheng says one wears fine hemp for three months, while Wang says one removes it when burial is completed. Again for a stepmother who remarries, Zheng says all wear mourning, while Wang says that only if one followed and was raised by her does one wear mourning. Again for a child who died young and for whom there is no mourning, Zheng says that for a child born one month, one cries one day; Wang says one day of crying replaces one month of mourning. Zheng and Wang each take the classics as ancestor and the commentaries as lineage, and each has differences. Xun Zhi collected antiquity and sought what was left, alternately reducing and increasing. From this we know that as the sages recede farther away, gaps and losses become more numerous. Therefore it is said that houses that assemble ritual are called gathered lawsuits; how could there be a fixed answer? Yet the three-year mourning for a mother while the father is alive has been practiced for more than forty years. It came from the generation of Gaozong the Great Emperor, not from the court of Empress Zetian. When the Great Emperor ruled and the palace submitted the document, the former deliberations could be put into practice; it was compiled into the regulations, and the mourning has been worn for a long time. What a former king approved was set out as law; what a later king approved was written as ordinance. Why must we oppose the former emperor's intent, block the feeling of a person's son, diminish a pure filial heart, and turn against the root of virtue and obligation? What harm is there to sage transformation? What disorder is there to the constant human order, that one would make the mourning one year, equal to that for paternal uncles' wives, and the same as for paternal aunts and sisters? The three-year mourning passes like a white colt through a crack; a gentleman mourning his parent has lifelong grief, how much more for two full cycles! Ritual is embodiment, practice, showing it by traces. Filial piety is storing up, nourishing, following it by the heart. Petty people are not ashamed of inhumanity and do not fear unrighteousness. Mourning dress has regulations to make foolish people reach upward; they are clothed in mourning garments so that seeing them produces crushing pain. Using this to guard people, there are still those who forget by evening one who died in the morning. Using this to regulate people, there are still those who remove mourning and follow auspicious affairs. Now we are gradually returning to ancient simplicity and must deepen filial piety and obligation. Restraining the worthy and drawing in the foolish, in principle, depends on Ning Qi; eating rice and wearing brocade are things one cannot bear to hear. If ordinary affairs and court ceremony are all to follow the Zhou rites, then when ancient ministers saw the ruler, dukes, ministers, and great officers presented lambs, geese, jade tablets, and disks; why do we not follow this now? Zhou punishments used tattooing, nose-cutting, castration, and foot-cutting; why do we not carry them out now? Zhou had hou, dian, nan, and wei domains, and audiences and visits had fixed numbers; why do we not carry this out now? Zhou did not let one serve before fifty, and at seventy one did not enter court; why do we not follow this now? Zhou used jing, yi, qiu, and dian to establish taxation; why do we not carry this out now? Zhou had three elders and five grades, father dying and son succeeding; why do we not carry this out now? Zhou used caps, robes, fur garments, and chariots in battle; why do we not carry this out now? Zhou divided land and had five geng, and in village and school nourished the aged; why do we not carry this out now? Examples such as these cannot be fully stated. Why only in the matter of filial thought begrudge one year of mourning for one's mother? This can make the heart ache; this can make one wail. The Odes says: "Alas, alas, my father and mother, who bore me with toil." The Ritual says: "When a father loves his child, he loves the worthy and lowers the incapable; when a mother loves her child, if worthy she loves him, and if incapable she pities him." Ruan Sizong, an outstanding talent of Jin and lofty man beyond the world, considered the mother weightier than the father. Based on the thread counts of trimmed and unhemmed mourning, coarseness and fineness already descend. How can one bear for the term of mourning to be reduced to one year? Surely later men are not all ashamed before antiquity. Following antiquity is not necessarily right; following the present is not necessarily wrong. Again, those who share the cooking hearth wear fine hemp; this is a clear meaning of the ritual classics. Elder-brother's wife and younger-brother-in-law are kept distant and treated like people on the road. Drawing them in and advancing them extends by analogy. Nephews all wear hemp mourning, but a younger uncle does not wear fine hemp; the feeling of pushing away is more than enough, and the obligation of harmonizing kin is insufficient. Again the mother's brothers have feeling as close as Weiyang; Di Pu litigated his uncle's injustice, and the Ning family housed a nephew as minister. Since I come from them, obligation too is deep. Not sharing the honor of a mother's sister, they are thereby lowered to small-work mourning. According to the ancient rites, this conflicts with common feeling. Now lowering the maternal uncle while honoring the maternal aunt is to scorn the present and glorify antiquity. These are all Taizong's regulations and have been practiced for a hundred years; rashly cutting and restoring them truly creates doubt.

Again, those who share the cooking hearth wear fine hemp; this is a clear meaning of the ritual classics. Elder-brother's wife and younger-brother-in-law are kept distant and treated like people on the road. Drawing them in and advancing them extends by analogy. Nephews all wear hemp mourning, but a younger uncle does not wear fine hemp; the feeling of pushing away is more than enough, and the obligation of harmonizing kin is insufficient. Again the mother's brothers have feeling as close as Weiyang; Di Pu litigated his uncle's injustice, and the Ning family housed a nephew as minister. Since I come from them, obligation too is deep. Not sharing the honor of a mother's sister, they are thereby lowered to small-work mourning. According to the ancient rites, this conflicts with common feeling. Now lowering the maternal uncle while honoring the maternal aunt is to scorn the present and glorify antiquity. These are all Taizong's regulations and have been practiced for a hundred years; rashly cutting and restoring them truly creates doubt.

sentences.zh: 於是紛議不定。

translations.literal: Thereupon debate was unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Debate deadlocked.

sentences.zh: 履冰又上疏曰：「《禮》：父在，為母十一月而練，十三月而祥，十五月而禫，心喪三年。

translations.literal: Lübing again submitted a memorial, saying: "The Ritual: when the father is alive, for the mother eleven months then practice; thirteenth month auspicious; fifteenth month end-of-mourning; heart mourning three years.
translations.idiomatic: Lübing again submitted a memorial, saying: "The Ritual: when the father is alive, for the mother eleven months then practice; thirteenth month auspicious; fifteenth month end-of-mourning; heart mourning three years.

sentences.zh: 上元中，則天皇后上表，請同父沒之服，亦未有行。

translations.literal: In the Shangyuan era Empress Wu Zetian submitted a memorial requesting mourning the same as when the father is dead, yet it was still not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: In Shangyuan Wu had asked for mourning equal to a father's death, but it had not yet taken effect.

sentences.zh: 至垂拱年中，始編入格，易代之後，俗乃通行。

translations.literal: By the Chuigong era it was first entered into the administrative code; after the change of dynasty the custom then spread in practice.
translations.idiomatic: Only in Chuigong was it written into the code; after the dynastic shift the custom spread.

sentences.zh: 臣開元五年，頻請仍舊。

translations.literal: Your servant, in the fifth year of Kaiyuan, repeatedly asked to restore the old rule.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant, in the fifth year of Kaiyuan, repeatedly asked to restore the old rule.

sentences.zh: 恩敕並嫂叔舅姨之服，亦付所司詳議。

translations.literal: The gracious edict also entrusted mourning for sisters-in-law, younger uncles, and mother's brothers and sisters to the relevant offices for detailed deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The throne also sent mourning for sisters-in-law, younger uncles, and maternal kin to the relevant offices for review.

sentences.zh: 諸司所議，同異相參。

translations.literal: The offices' deliberations mixed agreement and difference.
translations.idiomatic: The offices split.

sentences.zh: 所司惟執齊斬之文，又曰亦合典禮。

translations.literal: The relevant office alone held to the text on hemmed and cut garments, and also said it accorded with canonical ritual.
translations.idiomatic: One office clung to the hemmed-sackcloth articles and called that canonical.

sentences.zh: 竊見新修之格，猶依垂拱之偽，致有祖父母安存，子孫之妻亡沒，下房筵幾，亦立再周，甚無謂也。

translations.literal: I observe that the newly revised code still follows the Chuigong error, so that when grandparents are alive and a grandson's wife dies, in the lower apartments a second full cycle is also observed—most meaningless.
translations.idiomatic: The new code still followed Chuigong's error: with grandparents alive and a grandson's wife dead, lower apartments sometimes observed a second full cycle—absurd.

sentences.zh: 據《周易·家人》卦云：『利女貞女正位於內，男正位於外。

translations.literal: According to the Changes, Family hexagram: 'It profits the woman's constancy; the woman holds correct position within, the man holds correct position without.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes, Family hexagram, says: constancy profits the woman; she holds correct position within, the man without.

sentences.zh: 男女正，天地之大義。

translations.literal: Man and woman correct—this is the great principle of Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Correct man and woman embody Heaven and Earth's great principle.

sentences.zh: 家人有嚴君焉，父母之謂也。

translations.literal: The family has a stern lord—this means father and mother.
translations.idiomatic: A household has a stern lord: father and mother.

sentences.zh: 父父、子子、兄兄、弟弟、夫夫、婦婦，家道正而天下正矣。』

translations.literal: Father as father, son as son, elder brother as elder brother, younger brother as younger brother, husband as husband, wife as wife—the family way is correct and the realm is correct.'
translations.idiomatic: Let fathers be fathers, sons be sons, elder brothers be elder brothers, younger brothers be younger brothers, husbands be husbands, and wives be wives—right the family and the realm follows.

sentences.zh: 《禮》：『女在室，以父為天；

translations.literal: The Ritual: 'A woman in the chamber takes the father as Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: The Ritual says: in the chamber a woman takes her father as Heaven;

sentences.zh: 出嫁，以夫為天。』

translations.literal: after marriage, she takes the husband as Heaven.'
translations.idiomatic: after marriage she takes her husband as Heaven.

sentences.zh: 又：『在家從父，出嫁從夫，夫死從子。』

translations.literal: Again: 'At home she follows the father; after marriage she follows the husband; when the husband dies she follows the son.
translations.idiomatic: Again: at home she follows the father, in marriage the husband, in widowhood the son.

sentences.zh: 本無自專抗尊之法。

translations.literal: Fundamentally there is no law of self-willed defiance of elders.
translations.idiomatic: There is no charter for defying elders on one's own.

sentences.zh: 即《喪服四制》云：『天無二日，土無二王，國無二君，家無二尊，以一理之也。

translations.literal: The Mourning Dress Four Principles says: 'Heaven has no two suns, earth no two kings, the state no two lords, the family no two elders—one principle governs.
translations.idiomatic: The Mourning Dress Four Principles says: Heaven has no two suns, earth no two kings, a state no two lords, a family no two elders—one principle rules all.

sentences.zh: 故父在為母服周者，避二尊也。』

translations.literal: Therefore when the father is alive mourning for the mother is one cycle—to avoid two elders.
translations.idiomatic: Hence while the father lives, mourning for the mother is one cycle—to avoid two elders in one house.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下正持家國，孝理天下，而不斷在宸衷，詳正此禮，無隨末俗，顧念兒女之情。

translations.literal: I bow and consider that Your Majesty rightly holds family and state and filially governs the realm, yet does not decide in the imperial heart and correct this ritual in detail—do not follow vulgar custom and indulge children's feelings.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty rightly orders family and state by filial rule, yet has not settled this rite in the imperial heart—do not follow custom and indulge a child's feeling alone.

sentences.zh: 臣恐後代復有婦奪夫政之敗者。」

translations.literal: Your servant fears that later ages will again have women who usurp their husbands' government."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant fears that later ages will again have women who usurp their husbands' government."

translations.literal: The memorial concluded."
translations.idiomatic: The memorial closed.

sentences.zh: 疏奏未報。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted and not answered.
translations.idiomatic: No answer came.

sentences.zh: 履冰又上奏曰：臣聞夫婦之道，人倫之始。尊卑法於天地，動靜合於陰陽，陰陽和而天地生成，夫婦正而人倫式序。自家刑國，牝雞無晨，四德之禮不愆，三從之義斯在。即《喪服四制》云：「天無二日，土無二王，國無二君，家無二尊，以一理之也。故父在為母服周者，見無二尊也。」准舊儀，父在為母一週除靈，再周心喪。父必三年而後娶者，達子之志焉。豈先聖無情於所生，固有意於家國者矣。原夫上元肇年，則天已潛秉政，將圖僭篡，預自崇先。請升慈愛之喪，以抗尊嚴之禮，雖齊斬之儀不改，而几筵之制遂同。數年之間，尚未通用。天皇晏駕，中宗蒙塵。垂拱之末，果行聖母之偽符；載初之元，遂啟易代之深釁。孝和雖名反正，韋氏復效晨鳴。孝和非意暴崩，韋氏旋即稱制。不蒙陛下英算，宗廟何由克復？《易》云：「臣弒其君，子弒其父，非一朝一夕之故。」其斯之謂矣。臣謹尋禮意，防杜實深，若不早圖刊正，何以垂戒於後？所以薄言禮教，請依舊章，恩敕通明，蒙付所司詳議。且臣所獻者，蓋請正夫婦之綱，豈忘母子之道。諸議多不討其本源，所非議者，大凡只論罔極之恩；喪也寧戚；禽獸識母而不識父；秦燔書後禮經殘缺，後儒纘集，不足可憑；豈得與伯叔母服同，豈得與姑姊妹制等；三王不相襲禮，五帝不相沿樂；齊斬足為升降，歲年何忍不同：此並道聽途說之言，未習先王之旨，又安足以議經邦理俗之禮乎？臣請據經義以明之。所云「罔極之恩」者，春秋祭祀，以時思之。君子有終身之憂，霜露之感，豈止一二周之服哉！故聖人恐有朝死而夕忘，曾鳥獸之不若，為立中制，使賢不肖共成文理而已。所云「喪也寧戚」者，孔子答林放之問。至如太奢太儉，太易太戚，皆非禮中。苟不得中，名為俱失，不如太儉太戚焉。毀而滅性，猶愈於朝死夕忘焉。此論臨喪哀毀之容，豈比於同宗異姓之服？所云「禽獸識母而不識父」者，禽獸群居而聚筜，而無家國之禮，少雖知親愛其母，長不解尊嚴其父。引此為諭則亦禽獸之不若乎！所云「秦燔書後禮經殘缺，後儒纘集，不足可憑」者，人間或有遺逸，豈亦家戶到而燔之？假若盡燔，苟不可信，則墳黃都謬，庠序徒立，非聖之談，復云安屬？所云「與伯叔姑姊服同」者，伯叔姑姊有筵杖之制、三年心喪乎？所云「五帝不相沿樂，不相襲禮」，誠哉是言！此是則天懷私苞禍之情，豈可復相沿樂襲禮乎？所云「齊斬足為升降」者，母齊父斬，不易之禮。按《三年問》云：「將由修飾之君子與，三年之喪，若駟之過隙，遂之，則是無窮也。然則何以周也？曰：至親以周斷。是何也？曰：天地則已易矣，四時則已變矣，其在天地之者，莫不更始焉，以是象之也。然則何以三年？曰：加重焉耳。」故父加至再周，父在為母加三年心喪。今者還同父沒之制，則尊厭之律安施？《喪服四制》又曰：「凡禮之大體，體天地，法四時，則陰陽，順人情，故謂之禮。」訾之者是不知禮之所由生。非徒不識禮之所由制，亦恐未達孝子之通義。臣謹按《孝經》，以明陛下孝治之合至德要道，請論世欲訾禮之徒。夫至德謂孝悌，要道謂禮樂。「移風易俗，莫善於樂，安上治民，莫善於禮。」又《禮》有「無體之禮，無聲之樂。」按《孝經援神契》云：「天子孝曰就，就之為言成也。天子德被天下，澤及萬物，始終成就，則其親獲安，故曰就也。諸侯孝曰度，度者法也。諸侯居國，能奉天子法度，得不危溢，則其親獲安，故曰度也。卿大夫孝曰譽，譽之為言名也。卿大夫言行佈滿，能無惡稱，譽達遐邇，則其親獲安，故曰譽也。士孝曰究，究者以明審為義。士始升朝，辭親入仕，能審資父事君之禮，則其親獲安，故曰究也。庶人孝曰畜，畜者含畜為義。庶人含情受朴，躬耕力作，以畜其德，則其親獲安，故曰畜也。」陛下以韋氏構逆，中宗降禍，宸衷哀憤，睿情卓烈。初無一旅之眾，遂殄九重之妖，定社稷於阽危，拯宗枝於塗炭。此陛下孝悌之至，通於神明，光於四海，無所不通。使諸侯得守其法度，卿大夫得盡其言行，士得資親以事君，庶人得用天而分地。此陛下無體之禮，以安上理人也。上元以來，政由武氏，文明之後，法在凶人。賊害宗親，誅滅良善，勳階歲累，酺赦年頻。佞之則榮華，正之則遷謫。神龍、景雲之際，其事尤繁；先天、開元之間，斯弊都革。此陛下之無聲之樂，以移風易俗也。臣前狀單略，議者未識臣之懇誠。謹具狀重進，請付中書門下商量處分。臣言若讜，然敢側足於軒墀；臣言不忠，伏請竄跡於荒裔。

translations.literal: Lu Lubing again submitted a memorial: Your servant has heard that the way of husband and wife is the beginning of human relations. Honored and lowly take law from Heaven and earth; movement and stillness accord with yin and yang. When yin and yang are harmonious, Heaven and earth generate and complete; when husband and wife are correct, human relations are thereby ordered. From regulating the family to governing the state, the hen has no morning cry; the rites of the four virtues do not fail, and the obligation of the three followings is here. The Four Mourning Systems says: "Heaven has no two suns, earth has no two kings, the state has no two rulers, and the household has no two honored ones; these are ordered by one principle. Therefore when the father is alive, one wears one-year mourning for the mother, showing that there are not two honored ones." According to the old ritual, when the father was alive, for the mother one removed the spirit seat after one cycle and observed inner mourning for two cycles. That the father must wait three years before marrying again expresses the son's intent. How could the former sages have had no feeling for the one who gave birth, when they were certainly intent on household and state? Looking back, in the first year of Shangyuan, Zetian had already secretly taken hold of government. Planning usurpation, she first honored her ancestors. She requested raising compassionate mourning to oppose the rites of reverence; although the forms of trimmed and unhemmed mourning were not changed, the system of mats and seats became the same. For several years it still was not generally used. The Heavenly Emperor died, and Zhongzong suffered dust and exile. At the end of Chuigong, the false tally of the Sage Mother was indeed carried out; in the first year of Zaichu, the deep provocation for changing dynasties was opened. Although Xiaohe was called a return to correctness, the Wei clan again imitated the morning cry. Xiaohe suddenly died contrary to expectation, and the Wei clan immediately took charge. Had it not been for Your Majesty's heroic planning, how could the ancestral temples have been restored? The Changes says: "When a minister murders his ruler or a son murders his father, it is not the cause of one morning or one evening." This is what it means. Your servant has carefully sought the meaning of ritual, and its guard and prevention are truly deep. If we do not early plan to cut and correct this, how can we transmit warning to later times? Therefore I briefly spoke of ritual teaching and requested following the old statutes. The gracious edict was penetrating and clear, and I received referral to the responsible offices for detailed deliberation. What your servant submitted was a request to correct the bond of husband and wife; how could it forget the way of mother and son? Most deliberations do not examine the root and source. What they criticize generally only discusses boundless grace, that in mourning one should prefer grief, that birds and beasts know their mothers but not their fathers, that after Qin burned the books the ritual classics were damaged and later Confucians compiled them and are not reliable, that how could it be the same mourning as for paternal uncles' wives, how could it equal the rules for paternal aunts and sisters, that the Three Kings did not inherit one another's rites and the Five Emperors did not follow one another in music, and that trimmed and unhemmed garments are enough for increase and reduction while one cannot bear for the years to differ. These are all words heard on the road, not practiced in the former kings' intent. How are they enough to discuss the rites that order the state and regulate custom? Your servant requests to rely on classic meaning to clarify it. As for what is called "boundless grace," spring and autumn sacrifices remember it by season. A gentleman has lifelong grief and the feeling of frost and dew; how could it stop with one or two cycles of mourning dress? Therefore sages feared that some would have a morning death and evening forgetfulness, worse than birds and beasts, and established a middle regulation, so that worthy and unworthy together completed pattern and principle. As for what is called "in mourning, prefer grief," this is Confucius answering Lin Fang's question. As for too extravagant and too frugal, too easy and too grief-stricken, all are not within the ritual mean. If one cannot attain the mean, both are called losses, though too frugal and too grief-stricken are better. Destroying oneself and extinguishing one's nature is still better than morning death and evening forgetfulness. This discusses the appearance of grief and self-damage when facing mourning; how can it be compared to mourning dress for the same lineage and different surnames? As for "birds and beasts know the mother but not the father," birds and beasts live in flocks and gather without the rites of household and state. When young, they may know to love their mothers, but when grown they do not understand honoring their fathers. If this is cited as an analogy, are we not worse than birds and beasts? As for "after Qin burned the books, the ritual classics were damaged, and later Confucians compiled them, so they cannot be relied upon," among people there may have been texts left or lost; did Qin burn them from house to house? Suppose they were all burned. If they cannot be trusted, then the ancient classics are all mistaken, schools stand in vain, and to what does talk that rejects the sages belong? As for "the same mourning as paternal uncles' wives and paternal aunts and sisters," do paternal uncles' wives, paternal aunts, and sisters have a system of mats and staffs or three years of inner mourning? As for "the Five Emperors did not follow one another in music and did not inherit one another's rites," true indeed are these words! This was Zetian's feeling of harboring selfishness and wrapping disaster; how could one again follow her music and inherit her rite? As for "trimmed and unhemmed are enough for increase and reduction," trimmed for mother and unhemmed for father is unchanging ritual. According to Questions on Three Years: "Is it because of cultivated gentlemen? Three years of mourning is like a team of four horses passing a crack; if one extended it, it would be endless. Then why stop with one year? It says: the closest kin are cut off by a year. Why is this? It says: Heaven and earth have already changed; the four seasons have already changed; among what is within Heaven and earth, nothing has not begun anew, and this is used to model it. Then why three years? It says: weight is added." Therefore for the father it is increased to two full cycles, and while the father is alive, for the mother it is increased by three years of inner mourning. If now it is returned to the rule for when the father has died, where will the law of honored suppression be applied? The Four Mourning Systems also says: "In general, the great body of ritual embodies Heaven and earth, takes law from the four seasons, follows yin and yang, and accords with human feeling; therefore it is called ritual." Those who criticize this do not know from what ritual is born. Not only do they not understand from what ritual is made; I also fear they have not grasped the general obligation of a filial son. Your servant has carefully examined the Classic of Filial Piety to make clear that Your Majesty's filial governance accords with utmost virtue and the essential way, and I request to discuss those in the age who wish to criticize ritual. Utmost virtue means filial piety and fraternal respect; the essential way means rites and music. "For changing customs, nothing is better than music; for securing superiors and governing the people, nothing is better than ritual." Also, the Ritual has "formless ritual and soundless music." According to the Filial Piety apocryphon Yuan Shen Qi: "The Son of Heaven's filial piety is called completion; completion means accomplishing. When the Son of Heaven's virtue covers All Under Heaven and his grace reaches the myriad things, beginning and end are accomplished, and then his parents obtain peace; therefore it is called completion. A feudal lord's filial piety is called measure; measure means law. When a feudal lord resides in his state and can uphold the Son of Heaven's laws and measures, not becoming endangered or overflowing, then his parents obtain peace; therefore it is called measure. A minister or great officer's filial piety is called reputation; reputation means name. When a minister or great officer's words and conduct spread fully and can have no evil name, and his reputation reaches far and near, then his parents obtain peace; therefore it is called reputation. A shi's filial piety is called investigation; investigation takes clarity and examination as its meaning. When a shi first enters court, leaves his parents and enters service, and can examine the rite of using the father as resource to serve the ruler, then his parents obtain peace; therefore it is called investigation. A commoner's filial piety is called storing up; storing up takes containing and preserving as its meaning. When a commoner contains feeling and receives simplicity, personally plowing and laboring in order to store up his virtue, then his parents obtain peace; therefore it is called storing up." Because the Wei clan plotted rebellion and Zhongzong suffered disaster, Your Majesty's imperial heart was grieved and angered, and your sagely feeling was outstanding and fierce. At first you had not even one brigade of troops, yet you destroyed the monster in the ninefold palace, fixed the altars of soil and grain in danger, and rescued the imperial branches from mire and ashes. This is the utmost of Your Majesty's filial piety and fraternal respect, penetrating to spirits and brightness, shining over the four seas, with nothing it does not reach. It lets feudal lords keep their laws and measures, ministers and great officers exhaust their words and conduct, shi use kinship to serve the ruler, and commoners use Heaven and divide earth. This is Your Majesty's formless ritual, by which you secure superiors and order the people. Since Shangyuan, government came from the Wu clan; after Wenming, law lay with cruel people. They harmed imperial kin, killed the good, accumulated merit ranks every year, and frequently held feasts and amnesties. To flatter them brought glory; to correct them brought demotion and exile. During Shenlong and Jingyun, these affairs were especially numerous; between Xiantian and Kaiyuan, these abuses were all reformed. This is Your Majesty's soundless music, by which you changed customs. Your servant's previous statement was brief, and the debaters did not understand my earnest sincerity. I have carefully prepared this statement and present it again, requesting that it be sent to the Secretariat-Chancellery for deliberation and disposition. If your servant's words are honest, then I dare stand beside the palace steps. If your servant's words are not loyal, I humbly request exile to the distant borders.

Your servant has carefully sought the meaning of ritual, and its guard and prevention are truly deep. If we do not early plan to cut and correct this, how can we transmit warning to later times? Therefore I briefly spoke of ritual teaching and requested following the old statutes. The gracious edict was penetrating and clear, and I received referral to the responsible offices for detailed deliberation. What your servant submitted was a request to correct the bond of husband and wife; how could it forget the way of mother and son? Most deliberations do not examine the root and source. What they criticize generally only discusses boundless grace, that in mourning one should prefer grief, that birds and beasts know their mothers but not their fathers, that after Qin burned the books the ritual classics were damaged and later Confucians compiled them and are not reliable, that how could it be the same mourning as for paternal uncles' wives, how could it equal the rules for paternal aunts and sisters, that the Three Kings did not inherit one another's rites and the Five Emperors did not follow one another in music, and that trimmed and unhemmed garments are enough for increase and reduction while one cannot bear for the years to differ. These are all words heard on the road, not practiced in the former kings' intent. How are they enough to discuss the rites that order the state and regulate custom? Your servant requests to rely on classic meaning to clarify it. As for what is called "boundless grace," spring and autumn sacrifices remember it by season. A gentleman has lifelong grief and the feeling of frost and dew; how could it stop with one or two cycles of mourning dress? Therefore sages feared that some would have a morning death and evening forgetfulness, worse than birds and beasts, and established a middle regulation, so that worthy and unworthy together completed pattern and principle. As for what is called "in mourning, prefer grief," this is Confucius answering Lin Fang's question. As for too extravagant and too frugal, too easy and too grief-stricken, all are not within the ritual mean. If one cannot attain the mean, both are called losses, though too frugal and too grief-stricken are better. Destroying oneself and extinguishing one's nature is still better than morning death and evening forgetfulness. This discusses the appearance of grief and self-damage when facing mourning; how can it be compared to mourning dress for the same lineage and different surnames? As for "birds and beasts know the mother but not the father," birds and beasts live in flocks and gather without the rites of household and state. When young, they may know to love their mothers, but when grown they do not understand honoring their fathers. If this is cited as an analogy, are we not worse than birds and beasts? As for "after Qin burned the books, the ritual classics were damaged, and later Confucians compiled them, so they cannot be relied upon," among people there may have been texts left or lost; did Qin burn them from house to house? Suppose they were all burned. If they cannot be trusted, then the ancient classics are all mistaken, schools stand in vain, and to what does talk that rejects the sages belong? As for "the same mourning as paternal uncles' wives and paternal aunts and sisters," do paternal uncles' wives, paternal aunts, and sisters have a system of mats and staffs or three years of inner mourning? As for "the Five Emperors did not follow one another in music and did not inherit one another's rites," true indeed are these words! This was Zetian's feeling of harboring selfishness and wrapping disaster; how could one again follow her music and inherit her rite? As for "trimmed and unhemmed are enough for increase and reduction," trimmed for mother and unhemmed for father is unchanging ritual. According to Questions on Three Years: "Is it because of cultivated gentlemen? Three years of mourning is like a team of four horses passing a crack; if one extended it, it would be endless. Then why stop with one year? It says: the closest kin are cut off by a year. Why is this? It says: Heaven and earth have already changed; the four seasons have already changed; among what is within Heaven and earth, nothing has not begun anew, and this is used to model it. Then why three years? It says: weight is added." Therefore for the father it is increased to two full cycles, and while the father is alive, for the mother it is increased by three years of inner mourning. If now it is returned to the rule for when the father has died, where will the law of honored suppression be applied? The Four Mourning Systems also says: "In general, the great body of ritual embodies Heaven and earth, takes law from the four seasons, follows yin and yang, and accords with human feeling; therefore it is called ritual." Those who criticize this do not know from what ritual is born. Not only do they not understand from what ritual is made; I also fear they have not grasped the general obligation of a filial son. Your servant has carefully examined the Classic of Filial Piety to make clear that Your Majesty's filial governance accords with utmost virtue and the essential way, and I request to discuss those in the age who wish to criticize ritual. Utmost virtue means filial piety and fraternal respect; the essential way means rites and music. "For changing customs, nothing is better than music; for securing superiors and governing the people, nothing is better than ritual." Also, the Ritual has "formless ritual and soundless music." According to the Filial Piety apocryphon Yuan Shen Qi: "The Son of Heaven's filial piety is called completion; completion means accomplishing. When the Son of Heaven's virtue covers All Under Heaven and his grace reaches the myriad things, beginning and end are accomplished, and then his parents obtain peace; therefore it is called completion. A feudal lord's filial piety is called measure; measure means law. When a feudal lord resides in his state and can uphold the Son of Heaven's laws and measures, not becoming endangered or overflowing, then his parents obtain peace; therefore it is called measure. A minister or great officer's filial piety is called reputation; reputation means name. When a minister or great officer's words and conduct spread fully and can have no evil name, and his reputation reaches far and near, then his parents obtain peace; therefore it is called reputation. A shi's filial piety is called investigation; investigation takes clarity and examination as its meaning. When a shi first enters court, leaves his parents and enters service, and can examine the rite of using the father as resource to serve the ruler, then his parents obtain peace; therefore it is called investigation. A commoner's filial piety is called storing up; storing up takes containing and preserving as its meaning. When a commoner contains feeling and receives simplicity, personally plowing and laboring in order to store up his virtue, then his parents obtain peace; therefore it is called storing up." Because the Wei clan plotted rebellion and Zhongzong suffered disaster, Your Majesty's imperial heart was grieved and angered, and your sagely feeling was outstanding and fierce. At first you had not even one brigade of troops, yet you destroyed the monster in the ninefold palace, fixed the altars of soil and grain in danger, and rescued the imperial branches from mire and ashes. This is the utmost of Your Majesty's filial piety and fraternal respect, penetrating to spirits and brightness, shining over the four seas, with nothing it does not reach. It lets feudal lords keep their laws and measures, ministers and great officers exhaust their words and conduct, shi use kinship to serve the ruler, and commoners use Heaven and divide earth. This is Your Majesty's formless ritual, by which you secure superiors and order the people. Since Shangyuan, government came from the Wu clan; after Wenming, law lay with cruel people. They harmed imperial kin, killed the good, accumulated merit ranks every year, and frequently held feasts and amnesties. To flatter them brought glory; to correct them brought demotion and exile. During Shenlong and Jingyun, these affairs were especially numerous; between Xiantian and Kaiyuan, these abuses were all reformed. This is Your Majesty's soundless music, by which you changed customs. Your servant's previous statement was brief, and the debaters did not understand my earnest sincerity. I have carefully prepared this statement and present it again, requesting that it be sent to the Secretariat-Chancellery for deliberation and disposition. If your servant's words are honest, then I dare stand beside the palace steps. If your servant's words are not loyal, I humbly request exile to the distant borders.

sentences.zh: 左散騎常侍元行沖奏議曰：「天地之性，惟人最靈者，蓋以智周萬物，惟睿作聖，明貴賤，辨尊卑，遠嫌疑，分情理也。

translations.literal: Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry Yuan Xingchong submitted a deliberation, saying: "Of Heaven and Earth's nature, only the human is most spiritual—because wisdom encompasses the ten thousand things, only the perspicacious become sage, discerning noble and base, distinguishing honored and humble, keeping distant what is suspect, dividing feeling and principle.
translations.idiomatic: Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry Yuan Xingchong submitted a deliberation, saying: "Of Heaven and Earth's nature, only the human is most spiritual—because wisdom encompasses the ten thousand things, only the perspicacious become sage, discerning noble and base, distinguishing honored and humble, keeping distant what is suspect, dividing feeling and principle.

sentences.zh: 是以古之聖人，征性識本，緣情制服，有申有厭。

translations.literal: Therefore the ancient sages examined nature to know the root, followed feeling to set garments—there is extension and there is reduction.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient sages read nature for the root and followed feeling to set garments—sometimes extending, sometimes reducing.

sentences.zh: 天父、天夫，故斬衰三年，情理俱盡者，因心立極也。

translations.literal: Heaven as father, Heaven as husband—therefore full sackcloth three years; where feeling and principle are both exhausted, the heart establishes the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven is father, Heaven is husband—hence three years' full sackcloth where feeling and principle are both spent, the heart sets the utmost limit.

sentences.zh: 生則齊體，死則同穴，比陰陽而配合，同兩儀而成化。

translations.literal: In life they share one body; in death one grave—matching yin and yang in union, forming transformation with the two principles.
translations.idiomatic: Alive they share one body; dead one grave—yin and yang paired, the two principles made whole.

sentences.zh: 而妻喪杖期，情禮俱殺者，蓋以遠嫌疑，尊乾道也。

translations.literal: Yet for a wife's mourning, staff for one year—where feeling and ritual are both reduced—is because one keeps distant what is suspect and honors the yang way.
translations.idiomatic: Yet a wife's death brings staff for one year—feeling and ritual both cut—to keep distance from suspicion and honor the yang way.

sentences.zh: 父為嫡子三年斬衰，而不去職者，蓋尊祖重嫡，崇禮殺情也。

translations.literal: A father for the legitimate son wears three years' full sackcloth yet does not leave office—because one honors the grandfather and values the legitimate line, exalting ritual and reducing feeling.
translations.idiomatic: A father wears three years' full sackcloth for a legitimate son yet does not leave office—honoring the grandfather, weighting the legitimate line, exalting ritual over feeling.

sentences.zh: 資於事父以事君，孝莫大於嚴父。

translations.literal: Taking service to the father as service to the lord—no filial piety is greater than honoring the father.
translations.idiomatic: Serving the lord as one serves the father—no filial piety exceeds honoring the father.

sentences.zh: 故父在，為母罷職齊周而心喪三年，謂之尊厭者，則情申而禮殺也。

translations.literal: Therefore when the father is alive, for the mother one leaves office for hemmed sackcloth one cycle and heart mourning three years—called honored reduction: feeling is extended but ritual is reduced.
translations.idiomatic: So while the father lives, for the mother one leaves office, wears hemmed sackcloth one cycle, and heart-mourns three years—honored reduction: feeling extended, ritual cut.

sentences.zh: 斯制也，可以異於飛走，別於華夷。

translations.literal: This system can distinguish one from birds and beasts and set one apart from the civilized and the barbarian.
translations.idiomatic: That system separates humans from beasts and the civilized from the barbarian.

sentences.zh: 羲、農、堯、舜，莫之易也；

translations.literal: Xi, Nong, Yao, and Shun—none altered it;
translations.idiomatic: Xi, Nong, Yao, and Shun never altered it;

sentences.zh: 文、武、周、孔，同所尊也。

translations.literal: Wen, Wu, Zhou, and Confucius honored it alike.
translations.idiomatic: Wen, Wu, the Zhou, and Confucius honored it alike.

sentences.zh: 今若舍尊厭之重，虧嚴父之義，略純素之嫌，貽非聖之責，則事不師古，有傷名教矣。

translations.literal: If now one abandons the weight of honored reduction, injures the principle of honoring the father, overlooks the suspicion of plain white garments, and invites the blame of being un-sage-like, then affairs do not take the ancients as teachers and name-teaching is wounded.
translations.idiomatic: To cast off honored reduction, wound reverence for the father, ignore the suspicion plain garments guard against, and invite the charge of defying the sages would abandon the ancients and harm moral teaching.

sentences.zh: 姨兼從母之名，即母之女黨，加於舅服，有理存焉。

translations.literal: The mother's sister shares the name of the mother's sister—she is the mother's female kindred; increasing mourning for the mother's brother has reason in it.
translations.idiomatic: A mother's sister shares the mother's sister's name—she is the mother's female line; raising mourning for a mother's brother has its reason.

sentences.zh: 嫂叔不服，避嫌疑也。

translations.literal: Sister-in-law and younger uncle do not wear mourning—to avoid suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Sisters-in-law and younger uncles wore no mourning—to avoid suspicion.

sentences.zh: 若引同爨之緦，以忘推遠之跡，既乖前聖，亦謂難從。

translations.literal: If one cites finest hemp for sharing the hearth and forgets the trace of pushing distant, it both departs from former sages and is hard to follow.
translations.idiomatic: To cite finest hemp for sharing a hearth and forget the rule of pushing kin distant both departs from the sages and is hard to follow.

sentences.zh: 謹詳三者之疑，並請依古為當。」

translations.literal: We respectfully examine the doubts in all three cases and together request that following the ancient is correct."
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully examine the doubts in all three cases and together request that following the ancient is correct."

sentences.zh: 自是百僚議意不決。

translations.literal: From this the hundred officials' deliberations did not decide.
translations.idiomatic: The bureaucracy still could not settle.

sentences.zh: 至七年八月，下敕曰：「惟周公制禮，當歷代不刊；況子夏為《傳》，乃孔門所受。格條之內，有父在為母齊衰三年，此有為而為，非尊厭之義。與其改作，不如師古，諸服紀宜一依《喪服》文。」自是卿士之家，父在為母行服不同：或既周而禫，禫服六十日釋服，心喪三年者；

translations.literal: By the eighth month of the seventh year, an edict was issued: "Only the rites made by the Duke of Zhou should remain unaltered through successive ages; how much more since Zixia made the commentary, receiving it from Confucius's school. Within the regulations there is three-year trimmed mourning for a mother while the father is alive; this is something done for a particular purpose, not the meaning of honored suppression. Rather than changing and remaking it, it is better to take antiquity as teacher. The various mourning regulations should all follow the text of the Mourning Dress." From this time, in the households of ministers and grandees, mourning for a mother while the father was alive was carried out differently: some, after one cycle and the end-of-mourning rite, wore end-of-mourning garments for sixty days and then removed mourning, while observing inner mourning for three years;
translations.idiomatic: By the eighth month of the seventh year, an edict was issued: "Only the rites made by the Duke of Zhou should remain unaltered through successive ages; how much more since Zixia made the commentary, receiving it from Confucius's school.
